name: What should I do first if I want to turn my closed-off kitchen into an open-concept space?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if I want to turn my closed-off kitchen into an open-concept space?

acceptedAnswer.text:
## Direct answer
Start with a measured existing floor plan, a list of goals, and an early check of which walls carry loads or contain utilities. Removing a wall can affect structure, electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, and permit requirements.

## Context
An open-concept kitchen is more than demolition: the new layout must support cooking, circulation, storage, dining, and sightlines. In San Diego County, regulated structural, electrical, plumbing, gas, or mechanical work generally requires permit review before construction begins.

## Key factors
- Wall framing, beams, posts, and foundation conditions.
- Sink, range, dishwasher, and refrigerator locations.
- Window and door clearances.
- Ventilation, lighting, and panel capacity.

## Practical guidance
Bring room measurements, photos, appliance dimensions, and any prior plans to the consultation. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate design development, 3D visualization, permitting, construction, and final inspection as the scope requires.

## Soft positioning
A coordinated design-build plan helps connect the desired look with the construction work needed to make it function.
acceptedAnswer.description: Begin with an existing floor plan and a structural review—not demolition. Identify load-bearing walls, utilities, appliance locations, ventilation, and permit needs before selecting finishes. Photos, measurements, appliance dimensions, and any original plans will make the first design discussion more productive.
